titles: Is a Second Job Worth It in Canada? $10,000 Extra, You Keep $6,654
Side Job Math: Tax + Benefit Cuts Take a Third (Canada 2026)
The Tax Bracket Says 86%. The Real Number Is 2/3.
yt.description:
A weekend job: $10,000 more. The tax bracket says you keep 86%. The real number is closer to two thirds.

Example (federal only, 2026): Kai's family, two kids, family net income $50,000 → $60,000.
• Federal tax: 14%, and the last $1,477 (above $58,523) at 20.5% → $1,496
• Canada Child Benefit: with two kids it shrinks by 13.5% of the extra → $1,350 a year less
• Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit: 5% of the extra → $500 a year less
Total: $3,346 (33.5%) → you keep $6,654.

The twist: that's a third gone before provincial tax, CPP and EI, and the benefit cuts land the next July (they're based on last year's return).

Before you say yes, count the benefits, not just the bracket.

Next: part-time or full-time, which pays more after benefits?

Sources: CRA 2026 federal rates; canada.ca CCB and CGEB how much you can get (July 2026–June 2027); Budget 2026. Example; benefit thresholds are re-indexed each July. General information, not advice.
